title: Capturing URL Parameters
description: Pass dynamic parts of the URL to your views using converters.

slides.title: Dynamic URLs 🎯
slides.content: Often you want URLs that contain variable parts, like `/blog/5/` where 5 is a post ID. Django's path converters allow you to capture these values and pass them to your view as arguments.

slides.title: Using Converters
slides.codeSnippet:
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    # Capture an integer
    path('articles/<int:year>/', views.year_archive),
    # Capture a string
    path('articles/<str:slug>/', views.article_detail),
    # Capture a path (including slashes)
    path('pages/<path:page_path>/', views.page),
]

slides.title: View with Captured Parameters
slides.content: The view receives the captured values as arguments:

quizData.question: If you have a URL pattern `path('user/<int:user_id>/', views.profile)`, what type will the `user_id` parameter be in the view?
quizData.explanation: The `int` converter automatically converts the captured value to an integer before passing it to the view.

slides.title: Optional Parameters
slides.content: You can make parts of the URL optional using regular expressions or by providing default values in the view. For example:
slides.codeSnippet:
path('blog/<int:year>/', views.archive),
path('blog/', views.archive, {'year': 2025}),  # default year

def archive(request, year=2025):
    ...

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `slug` for SEO‑friendly URLs

Slugs are strings that can contain letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. They're great for article titles: `my-first-post`.
